findings.text: follow-on: the lift_id branch of clear() ignores the group argument and matches on id alone, so clear(config, group="totally-different-group", lift_id=<a codex-sub lift>) returned the codex-sub lift's id and cleared it — reproduced against a temp record. A caller that passes a group and an id gets a cross-group revocation with no error, and the CLI follow-on that wires --clear --group would inherit the footgun.

follow-on: _lift_by_id consults no expiry, so clear(..., lift_id=...) revokes a record that is no longer in force (past its at, or older than max_hours) and stamps cleared_at on a dead lift, whereas the session/group path resolves only an in-force lift via _governing_lift; the docstring's Revoke an in-force lift therefore does not hold for the id path.

follow-on: budget.lift.max_multiple and max_hours carry their 3.0/168 defaults only in ceilings()'s code fallback, while every other budget block default (pace_multiple, drain_lead_hours, resume_reserve_pct) is declared in the shipped defaults layer; a fresh install reaches the ceilings through the resolver rather than the data layer.

item_verdicts.diff: Read line by line. clear() gains lift_id and session keywords; the lift_id branch resolves through a new _lift_by_id (id match only), the else branch calls _governing_lift(session=session), and both are gated by a cleared_at check. effective_budget drops the os.environ RECKON_SESSION read and returns configured_pace_multiple(config) for the non-multiple forms. configured_pace_multiple now delegates to pace_module.policy(config).pace_multiple, which reads the same budget.pace_multiple block with the same 1.1 default the removed DEFAULT_PACE_MULTIPLE carried. The LiftConfig class and budget.lift slots are added to flight.yaml and regenerated. Two defects in the new code are below; the four closed findings are genuinely closed.
item_verdicts.done_when: Reproduced at head 276f4a381. I re-ran the gate at head: tests/test_budget_lift.py+test_flight.py+test_flight_lanes.py+test_budget_group.py+test_bookend_reserve_by_group.py+test_pace.py gave 166 passed, EXIT=0, matching the manifest's after_suite. The manifest's baseline_suite records the same six files at base 5a9aadbf5 as 154 passed, EXIT=0; both are completed:true with zero failures, so added_failure_count is 0 and added_failure_ids is one test's worth of nothing. The negative control is sound: mutating clear()'s session=session to session=None in a scratch copy reddens exactly tests/test_budget_lift.py::test_clear_with_a_session_revokes_that_session_lift_leaving_the_global (1 failed, 165 passed, EXIT=1), a test the head arm passes, and the failing id is the one the session-clearing assertion names. Each of the four closed findings carries a new test, and test_flight.py's byte-identical regeneration assertion covers the schema declaration.
item_verdicts.goal: This node answers the five follow-on findings the prior review (r-20261008T132610418827) raised against the §10 lift resolver. It closes four: clear() now names the lift it revokes (by lift_id, or by session, where a session's own lift governs it over a global one and a bare clear still revokes only a global lift); effective_budget no longer returns a None pace_multiple for the drain-by and uncapped forms, keeping the configured multiple instead; configured_pace_multiple reads through pace.policy so it shares one default with the allowance derivation; and budget.lift.max_multiple/max_hours are declared flight keys, regenerated into _flight_schema.py and flight.schema.json, so a layer setting max_multiple=2 refuses a 2.5 lift and one at max_hours=24 makes a 30 h lift inert. The fifth follow-on (the three readers' wiring, the crew budget CLI, pace_hold.releases_at, pace.lift_id on dispatch rows, follower lines, the skill fence and help-contract tests) is explicitly out of scope and named in follow_ons, so a granted lift still changes no dispatch decision end to end. One residual defect remains in the new clear() id path (below), and the shipped ceilings defaults sit in the resolver fallback rather than the defaults layer.
item_verdicts.manifest: Read. Carries the revision pair (base 5a9aadbf5, head 276f4a381), baseline_suite and after_suite as proper JSON with completed:true, exit 0 and failure_count 0, and a negative_control_log whose last line is a bare EXIT=1. The claim that the env read left effective_budget is verifiable in the diff (the RECKON_SESSION branch and SESSION_ENV constant are removed) and pinned by test_effective_budget_ignores_a_session_environment_variable.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git diff 5a9aadbf5..276f4a381 lists six paths, all inside the node's declared write paths: reckon/crew/budget_lift.py, reckon/schema/flight.yaml, reckon/_flight_schema.py, docs/_shared/flight.schema.json, tests/test_budget_lift.py and docs/evidence/fragments/a-window-paces-the-lane/the-lift-record-answers-its-review.html. No plan state, index or sprint file is touched; the manifest's follow_ons names the out-of-scope remainder rather than half-building it.
